deployment_recommendation: BLOCK — overall score 35/100 is below the 60-point deployment threshold. Resolve all P1 gaps before promoting to production.

gaps.gap_detail: Without agent telemetry there is no basis for anomaly detection or post-incident forensics.
Prompt injection and goal hijacking are invisible without gateway-level logging.

gaps.control: Behavioral baselines established for each agent
gaps.gap_detail: Anomaly detection is impossible without a baseline — every alert will be a false positive or missed entirely.

gaps.control: Log retention >= 72 hours at full fidelity
gaps.gap_detail: Most AI incidents are detected hours after the triggering event — 72h retention is the minimum for viable forensics.

gaps.control: Rollback procedure tested within last 90 days
gaps.gap_detail: Untested rollbacks routinely fail under incident conditions — the most common readiness gap.

gaps.control: Rollback time < 30 minutes — documented and verified
gaps.gap_detail: Rollbacks that take hours extend the blast radius of an active incident significantly.
Without a kill switch, containing a rogue or hijacked agent requires manual intervention that takes minutes — not seconds.

gaps.control: Kill switch tested in staging environment
gaps.gap_detail: Kill switches that exist in code but have never fired in the target environment routinely fail at the worst moment.
Multi-agent collusion or a shared injection vector may require halting the entire agent fleet at once.

gaps.control: Kill switch activation time < 60 seconds — verified
gaps.gap_detail: A 5-minute kill time allows a rogue agent to exfiltrate gigabytes or spawn dozens of subprocesses before containment.

gaps.control: Network egress policies restrict agent outbound traffic
gaps.gap_detail: Without egress restrictions, any injected instruction can exfiltrate data to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

gaps.control: IR playbooks mapped to each AI threat type
gaps.gap_detail: General IT IR playbooks do not cover AI-specific containment steps (session flushing, kill switch activation, RAG corpus rollback).

gaps.control: Team trained on AI-specific IR playbooks
gaps.gap_detail: Playbooks that only the author understands are useless during a 2am incident with the author unavailable.

gaps.control: Approvals workflow configured for sensitive containment actions
gaps.gap_detail: Without an approvals workflow, containment actions taken under pressure have no audit trail and no second pair of eyes.

gaps.control: Incident command structure defined for AI incidents
gaps.gap_detail: AI incidents without a command structure devolve into coordination failures — multiple people taking conflicting containment actions.

gaps.control: AI IR playbook tested in a tabletop exercise
gaps.gap_detail: Untested playbooks always have gaps — tabletop exercises surface them before a real incident does.
